g9-geography-ug7-t1.overview: Soil Degradation and Conservation sits inside Contemporary Geographic Issues and Public Concerns in Ethiopia. Natural resource degradation is the focus of Unit 7 of Grade 9 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the unit traces how erosion, deforestation, and pollution drive natural resource degradation across the highlands. Then it sets out the conservation measures, from terracing to reforestation, that slow the damage. Next, it presents the Green Legacy tree-planting movement of 2019, then points ahead to Unit 8: Geographic Inquiry Skills and Techniques. Students will also learn how natural resource degradation applies to real-life situations such as farming, water supply, and food security.
objectives: Describe the natural and human causes of soil erosion.
Explain the conservation measures that reduce natural resource degradation.
Compare reforestation and afforestation as forest remedies.
Analyze the threats to the country’s water resources.
Finally, describe the aims of the Green Legacy movement.
g9-geography-ug7-t1.simple:
Soil Degradation and Conservation in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, soil erosion by running water as the country’s main soil problem.
  • Then the human causes, from deforestation and overgrazing to poor tillage.
  • Also the fixes, terracing, contour ploughing, strip cultivation, and check dams.
g9-geography-ug7-t1.detailed:
Soil Degradation and Conservation — the essentials. First, soil erosion by running water as the country’s main soil problem. Then the human causes, from deforestation and overgrazing to poor tillage. Also the fixes, terracing, contour ploughing, strip cultivation, and check dams.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe the natural and human causes of soil erosion.
  • Explain the conservation measures that reduce natural resource degradation.
  • Compare reforestation and afforestation as forest remedies.
  • Analyze the threats to the country’s water resources.
  • Finally, describe the aims of the Green Legacy movement.
